title: Microsoft Teams: connect a meeting to an existing Planner plan
summary: The briefing passes: its planned behaviour, default availability and rollout dates match Microsoft's notice and roadmap. The documented controls and product licensing are supported, and the briefing explicitly reports Microsoft's conflicting navigation and entitlement descriptions.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let users connect Teams meetings to existing Planner plans.
claims.quote: With this capability, users can now connect Teams meetings to existing Planner plans, so all related tasks across meetings can be tracked in one place.

claims.claim: Teams meetings currently create separate Planner plans automatically for meeting tasks.
claims.quote: Teams meetings automatically create a corresponding Planner plan to capture meeting tasks.

claims.claim: Tasks for a long-running initiative can become scattered across auto-generated plans.
claims.quote: However, when teams use meetings as their primary collaboration surface for long-running initiatives, tasks from the same project can become scattered across multiple auto-generated plans.

claims.claim: The identity Facilitator uses to write tasks to a linked plan is not described.
claims.quote: Searched: Facilitator Planner meeting selected plan task permissions identity access license meter. Read facilitator-teams, manage-planner-app and the notice; results described notes storage and general Planner access, not the linked-plan task-writing identity.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page describes connecting a meeting to an existing Planner plan at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "meeting" "existing Planner" plan connect licensing admin disable; Teams meeting connect existing Planner plan tenant control PowerShell Graph disable linking 561490. Read facilitator-teams and manage-planner-app; no feature-specific Learn page returned.

claims.quote: Searched: Facilitator Planner meeting selected plan task permissions identity access license meter. Read facilitator-teams, planner/licensing and the Planner service description; the latter mentions metered Planner APIs, not a meter for the meeting-linking option.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Facilitator setup page documents Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: select Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Facilitator from the app list. ... In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> is the documented MicrosoftTeams app-state operation.
claims.quote: This cmdlet updates app state and app available values for the Microsoft Teams app. ... -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app. ... -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant. ... Type: Boolean

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Planner > Block turns off the Planner app at organisation level.
claims.quote: go to Teams apps > Manage apps. ... To turn off Planner for your organization, search for the Planner app, select it, and then select Block.

claims.where: controls[1].api; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false is documented under turning off Planner for the organisation.
claims.quote: If you're a global admin and you want to turn off Microsoft Planner for your organization, you can use Windows PowerShell. ... Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false

claims.claim: No documented setting specifically turns off connecting meetings to existing Planner plans.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting connect existing Planner plan tenant control PowerShell Graph disable linking 561490. Read facilitator-teams, manage-planner-app, manage-apps, disable-planner and returned references; channel-plan controls and plan deletion operations do not govern meeting linking.

claims.claim: The Facilitator setup page says Facilitator is allowed by default.
claims.quote: Facilitator is allowed by default.

claims.claim: The setup page qualifies that default by saying Facilitator is blocked if all apps are blocked.
claims.quote: However, if all apps are blocked for your organization, Facilitator is also blocked.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference labels its -IsBlocked $true example as unblocking.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true ... Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: The app-management page instead places Facilitator at Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents > Facilitator > Edit availability, allowing availability to no one.
claims.quote: Built-in Teams agents like Channel Agent, Facilitator ... are managed from the Built-In Teams agents page, not the Manage apps page. ... Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents. ... select one or more agents and choose Edit availability. ... or to no one.

claims.claim: The Facilitator setup page asks administrators to sign in with Teams admin credentials.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center with your Teams admin credentials.

claims.claim: The Planner PowerShell disable page applies to basic plans in Teams and web.
claims.quote: This article applies to: Basic plans in the Planner app in Teams and Web

claims.claim: The Planner PowerShell disable page applies to all plans in other Planner endpoints.
claims.quote: All plans in other Planner endpoints (including Planner mobile, and Planner connectors).

claims.claim: The Planner PowerShell page is written for a global admin.
claims.quote: If you're a global admin and you want to turn off Microsoft Planner for your organization, you can use Windows PowerShell.

claims.claim: The disable-Planner page inconsistently introduces the disable command as turning off Outlook calendar sync.
claims.quote: Turn off Planner for your organization using PowerShell ... Open PowerShell and run the following command to turn off Outlook calendar sync for Planner: Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false

claims.claim: The briefing does not establish Update-M365TeamsApp as automation for the Built-in Teams agents route.
claims.quote: Searched: Update-M365TeamsApp Facilitator built-in Teams agents IsBlocked automation. Read update-m365teamsapp and manage-apps: the former documents Teams app state, the latter built-in agent UI; neither explicitly connects this command to the built-in agent route.
